purpose: The single vocabulary of states used across the knowledge base. Two different things are tracked: how far a *curriculum item* (a topic, skill or competency) has been developed, and whether a *content artefact* (a lesson, exercise set or interactive) may be shown as verified. Mixing the two is how platforms end up presenting drafts as finished courses, so they are kept apart.

proficiency_levels.definition: Can describe what the concept is, where it is used and why it exists.
proficiency_levels.evidence: Short conceptual answer, no formal derivation.

proficiency_levels.definition: Can apply the concept to standard problems with reference material available.
proficiency_levels.evidence: Guided exercises, code that runs on supplied data.

proficiency_levels.definition: Can select and apply the concept independently to a new problem, and explain the choice.
proficiency_levels.evidence: Independent exercises, implementation from scratch, comparison of alternatives.

proficiency_levels.definition: Can derive, justify, debug and critique the concept, including its limits and failure modes.
proficiency_levels.evidence: Derivations, counterexamples, debugging, design review of trade-offs.

topic_status.description: State of a curriculum item (SK-*, competency, module). Every item in the knowledge base carries exactly one.

values.identified: Discovered in a roadmap or proposed by the competency audit. Nothing else has happened yet.
values.gap_under_review: Believed to matter but not yet judged essential/recommended/optional, or its position in the path is unsettled.
values.awaiting_sources: Scope, prerequisites and importance are recorded; no approved primary source has been supplied for it.
values.sources_indexed: One or more supplied sources are identified, hashed and mapped to this item's sections.
values.content_in_development: Lessons are being written against indexed sources.
values.in_verification: A draft exists and is being checked for source fidelity, correctness, pedagogy and assessment quality.
values.verified: Required checks have passed; remaining limitations are written down in a verification record.
values.published: Verified and reachable in the learner-facing interface.
values.needs_revision: A check failed or a reviewer raised an issue; the item is not to be shown as verified.
values.stale: A source, prerequisite or competency changed after verification, so the earlier verification no longer applies.
values.out_of_scope: Deliberately not part of the current learning path; the reason is recorded.

transition_rules: sources_indexed requires: at least one source registered in knowledge/sources with a hash, and a section-level mapping for the item.
content_in_development requires: every lesson learning objective traceable to a mapped source section or an explicitly labelled supplemental reference.
in_verification requires: exercises have defined expected outcomes and solutions or rubrics.
verified requires: a verification record naming the checks that ran, their results, and the checks that did not run.
published requires: verified plus rendering and navigation checks on the live interface.

publication_state.description: State of a content artefact (lesson, exercise set, interactive) as it appears to the learner.

values.draft: Written but not checked. Must be labelled as unverified wherever it is visible.
values.in_verification: Under active checking; not to be presented as verified.
values.needs_revision: A check failed; the specific issue is recorded and visible.
values.verified: Source fidelity, technical correctness, pedagogy and assessment checks passed, with the verification record attached.
values.published: Verified and included in the learner-facing build.
values.stale: An upstream source or competency changed after the last verification.

publication_state.display_rule: The interface must derive its verification badge from this field. Unverified content must never render as verified, and a lesson with no verification record must render as draft.

verification_status.description: Outcome of an individual check, so that partial verification is representable.
blocked_examples: Code execution unavailable in the checking environment.
A cited external source could not be retrieved; its content is not asserted.
verification_status.partial_definition: Some of the check's criteria were met and the unmet part is named in the record. 'partial' is never treated as a pass: a verification record whose outcome is 'verified' may not contain a partial or not_run core check.
